READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

- file: qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:321
- category: dead-code
- title: Redundant memset(sp, 0, sizeof(*sp)) at the top of drain_state_into
- detail: drain_state_into zeroes the caller's output struct at line 321, then builds the entire state in a zero-initialized local (line 322: struct hybrid_state_v1 s = {0}) and unconditionally copies it out at line 473 (*sp = s) - the only paths that skip line 473 call exit(2) (lines 432, 495-499 are in callees that terminate the process), and the sole caller drain_state_to_file (line 508) reads the struct only after the call returns. hybrid_state_v1 is padding-free by design (include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h asserts every field offset), so the {0} local plus struct assignment already determines every output byte; the memset writes bytes that are always overwritten.
- claimed safety: The memset's effect is fully shadowed by the unconditional *sp = s on every returning path; removing it cannot change any byte of the written state file.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. 204	// 0xE0500000 (DS220 24.2). The documented register window spans offset

input.reason: Verified all four legs of the claim. (1) drain_state_into is static with exactly one caller (hybrid_handoff.c:508); grep across andesim, andesim-demo, and vsim_andesim finds no other source reference. (2) The function body has no return/goto and the plugin has no setjmp/longjmp; the only path skipping the unconditional '*sp = s' at line 473 is exit(2) at line 432, which kills the process before the caller could read the struct. (3) hybrid_state_v1 is provably padding-free: the sum of all member sizes (7504 bytes) equals the sizeof locked by state_abi_check.h:106, and every field offset is asserted - so 's = {0}' plus the explicit assignments determine every byte, and the struct assignment copies every byte (the C padding-bytes-unspecified caveat has nothing to apply to). (4) The caller reads the struct only after the call returns, writing exactly sizeof bytes to the file. The memset at line 321 is therefore fully shadowed on every observable path; removing it cannot change the state file bytes, sidecars, log output, or exit codes.
